notes: kî → 'For that' is one two-word rendering of a single connective morpheme (rule 55), headed on the coordinator.

The verse writes two 'of's and has two licensors: the first reaches the verb's bare object and joins the verb's unit (rule 44), the second is the quantifying chain's own relation and belongs to the rectum (rule 19). The competing reading ('any of' as one quantifier) is named in the unit note.
maddûaʿ has an English word of its own, so the fronted 'dost' is the verb's under rule 17's second limit rather than the interrogative's.
